Complete files, clear status and collections that respect the borrower

For NBFCs, housing finance and gold loan companies, microfinance lenders and loan DSAs, we connect the LOS, LMS and messaging so inquiries get honest eligibility guidance, files arrive complete, borrowers always know where they stand, and reminders and collections stay within RBI's conduct rules.

What makes lending & NBFCs different

  • Applications stall on missing or unreadable documents, and credit teams spend hours chasing files instead of assessing them.

  • Borrowers call branches and DSAs for status because nothing updates them, and some move to a faster lender.

  • Reminder and collection contact must follow RBI rules on hours, language, agent notice and harassment, and messy dialer data makes that hard to evidence.

  • Top-up offers go out from spreadsheets without a recorded credit approval or marketing consent.

  • Retail and MSME loans need a KFS before signing, and digital journeys add cooling-off terms, a stated purpose for each consent and data kept on servers in India.

Where automation helps lending & NBFCs

  • Indicative eligibility and lead routing

    Inquiries from campaigns, aggregators, DSAs and WhatsApp are checked against your published criteria and routed to the right branch, relationship manager or digital journey, with no promise of approval, rate or limit.

  • Document and KYC tracking

    Product-wise checklists, secure uploads or DigiLocker and CKYC fetch through your own integrations, AI checks for blur and mismatches confirmed by operations, and Video KYC slots tracked to completion.

  • Status updates, KFS and cooling-off tracking

    Borrowers hear about every milestone, receive the KFS before they sign, see the cooling-off window on digital loans, and get the main reasons in writing when an application is declined.

  • Pre-due reminders and conduct-safe collections

    Reminders before every EMI, same-day bounce notices, and overdue follow-up from 1600-series numbers within permitted hours and borrower preferences, with hardship cases routed to a trained officer.

  • Servicing assistant and early warning alerts

    Statements, foreclosure letters and NOCs requested through an assistant grounded in your documents, and fraud or early warning alerts summarized for the risk team to decide.

  • Top-ups and renewals approved by credit

    Review lists built from repayment behavior and approved by the credit team before consented outreach, with a fresh credit assessment and a KFS for every top-up or gold loan renewal.

Discover and inquireStandard3–5 weeks

Inquiry desk with indicative eligibility

Capture loan inquiries from ads, aggregators, the website, WhatsApp and DSAs, ask only what indicative eligibility needs, check it against the lender's published criteria, and route likely applicants to the right owner. It guides; it never decides.

Lending & NBFCs · Fintech & payments

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Loan inquiries arrive from campaigns, aggregators, DSAs and WhatsApp in different formats. Many fall outside the lender's serviceable areas or product rules, while good prospects wait hours for a callback and apply elsewhere. Sales staff sometimes over-promise approval or rates, which turns into complaints and mis-selling risk later.

Trigger

A new inquiry from a lead form, the lender's WhatsApp Business number, website chat, an aggregator feed or a DSA submission.

How it runs

  1. Capture the inquiry into one queue with source, product interest and the consent shown at that step. AI reads free-text messages for product and amount, and duplicates of existing customers or open applications are merged.
  2. Collect a short set of banded answers on a page on the lender's domain: pincode, product, amount range, age band, employment type and income band. No PAN, Aadhaar or bank details are requested at this stage.
  3. Check the answers against the lender's published criteria, such as serviceable pincodes, age, minimum income and product limits, and show a plainly worded result with the reason.
  4. Route likely applicants to the branch, relationship manager, DSA owner or digital application journey by product and location, with a summary of what was shared.
  5. On multi-lender platforms, display every matching offer that partner lenders return, with each lender's name, amount, tenor, APR and charges, without favoring any lender, as the Digital Lending Directions require.
  6. Send one approved follow-up template to opted-in prospects who have not applied, then close the inquiry with a reason code.

Human checkpoint

Indicative results never promise approval, a rate or a limit. Credit assessment, bureau checks and the decision stay with the lender's credit team after a full application, and sales staff take over whenever the prospect asks for a person or the case is unusual.

  • Inquiry-to-application conversion by source

Apply, verify and decideAdvanced6–10 weeks

Application, KYC and status tracker

Generate the right checklist for each application or proposal, collect documents through a secure page or DigiLocker, track KYC steps, chase what is missing, and keep the customer updated until a person makes the decision.

Lending & NBFCs · Insurance agencies & brokers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Loan files and insurance proposals wait on missing pages, unreadable scans, name mismatches, Video KYC slots and medical requirements. Operations teams chase items over phone and personal WhatsApp, credit and underwriting receive incomplete files, and customers who hear nothing call the branch, DSA or agent, or quietly go elsewhere.

Trigger

A new application in the LOS, a proposal logged in the broker or agency system, or a requirement raised by credit, underwriting or the insurer, read through the system's API or a scheduled export.

How it runs

  1. Build the checklist from product rules and applicant type, such as salaried, self-employed, proprietor, company or NRI, and send it with a secure link on the lender's or broker's own domain.
  2. Collect documents by upload, or fetch them from DigiLocker or CKYC where the regulated entity uses those routes, showing the purpose of each consent.
  3. Classify each document with AI and flag blur, expiry, missing pages and name or date mismatches for an operations officer to confirm.
  4. Track KYC status: CKYC record found, Video KYC booked and completed by the regulated entity's trained official, or additional verification needed.
  5. Chase missing items on the customer's chosen channel, and alert the file owner when a file ages past its target.
  6. Send status updates at each milestone: received, items pending, under review, approved, declined with the main reasons, disbursed or issued.
  7. Before a borrower signs, confirm the KFS reached them, and for digital loans log the cooling-off window the lender's board has set.

Human checkpoint

Operations officers verify documents and resolve KYC exceptions. Credit officers, underwriters or the insurer decide every application and record the reasons; the tracker never approves, declines, prices or sets limits.

Use and serviceAdvanced5–8 weeks

Servicing assistant grounded in approved documents

Answer policy, loan and investment servicing questions on WhatsApp and the website only from approved documents, with the source shown, and hand account requests, complaints and anything uncertain to a person with the context attached.

Insurance agencies & brokers · Lending & NBFCs · Wealth & investment advisory

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Customers ask the same questions about waiting periods, exclusions, foreclosure charges, statement downloads, nominee changes and capital gains statements. Answers vary by who picks up, wrong answers become complaints, and simple requests wait in the same queue as urgent ones.

Trigger

A customer messages the business's WhatsApp number or website chat, or emails the service inbox.

How it runs

  1. Verify the customer through the registered mobile number or an OTP on the business's own page before sharing any account-specific information.
  2. Answer general questions only from the approved document set, such as policy wordings, Customer Information Sheets, charges schedules, FAQs and process notes, and show the source.
  3. Turn account requests, such as statements, premium receipts, NOCs, foreclosure letters and nominee or address changes, into service tickets with the details captured.
  4. Hand over at once for complaints, claims, grievances, bereavement, suspected fraud, any question about what to buy or sell, or whenever the assistant is unsure.
  5. Log complaints with their timeline and tell the customer the escalation route that applies, such as the RBI Ombudsman, the Insurance Ombudsman or SEBI SCORES.
  6. Review unanswered and low-rated questions each month and update the document set with each document's owner.

Human checkpoint

Service staff own every account change, complaint and exception, and the grievance redressal officer owns escalations. The assistant gives no advice on products, cover, claim outcomes or investments.

Pay and renewStandard4–6 weeks

EMI reminders and respectful collections workflow

Remind borrowers before each EMI, flag mandate bounces the same day, and run overdue follow-up through approved channels within RBI's conduct rules, with hardship cases routed to a trained officer.

Lending & NBFCs · Fintech & payments

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Bounced NACH and UPI AutoPay debits surface late, reminders go out from dialer lists that ignore preferences and contact hours, and early-stage overdue customers get the same treatment as wilful defaulters. That raises complaints and conduct risk without improving recovery.

Trigger

A daily sync of installments due in the coming days from the LMS API or export, and mandate presentation results from the sponsor bank or payment gateway.

How it runs

  1. Send pre-due reminders in the borrower's language with amount, date and payment options by DLT SMS, email, app notification, or an approved WhatsApp utility template where the borrower opted in, with no offers that would make them promotional.
  2. Detect bounced debits the same day and send a factual notice by DLT SMS, email or app notification with a payment link on the lender's domain and charges as set in the loan agreement.
  3. Run overdue follow-up by SMS, email, app and calls from 1600-series numbers, since WhatsApp's policy lists debt collection as a prohibited use, and schedule calls only between 8 am and 7 pm, or narrower hours where rules or borrower preferences require.
  4. Flag hardship signals, such as job loss, illness or bereavement, and route them to a trained officer to discuss options under the lender's policy.
  5. When a recovery agent is assigned or changed, send the borrower the agent's details by SMS and email before any contact, and from January 2027 confirm the agent's certification first.
  6. Log every attempt, outcome and recording reference, and report any contact outside the rules to the collections head the same day.

Human checkpoint

Collections officers decide settlements, restructuring, waivers, agent assignment and any legal step. The workflow never threatens, never contacts relatives or references, and never sends legal notices on its own.

Claims, disputes and alertsAdvanced6–10 weeks

Fraud alert triage for analysts

Enrich every fraud or risk alert with customer, device and transaction context, summarize the evidence, prioritize the queue by severity and time sensitivity, and record each analyst decision to improve the rules.

Fintech & payments · Lending & NBFCs

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Rules and models raise more alerts than analysts can clear, and each review means opening the core system, device logs, past cases and KYC files. Urgent cases, such as an account takeover in progress or a mule account receiving funds, wait behind low-risk noise, and decisions are rarely recorded well enough to improve the rules.

Trigger

An alert from transaction monitoring, the risk engine or early warning signals on loans, or a fraud complaint received through the cybercrime reporting system.

How it runs

  1. Enrich the alert with account age, KYC status, device and login history, velocity, beneficiaries and linked accounts.
  2. Summarize the evidence with AI in a fixed format and suggest a priority with reasons, citing the data used.
  3. Queue alerts by severity and time sensitivity, and page the on-call analyst for alerts that need action within minutes.
  4. The analyst decides: release, contact the customer through a verified channel, hold or block within policy, or escalate to the fraud risk unit.
  5. Record the decision and reason, trigger customer messages from approved templates, and pass reportable cases to the officers who own fraud reporting and suspicious transaction reports.
  6. Review outcomes weekly with the risk team to retire noisy rules and adjust thresholds.

Human checkpoint

Fraud analysts decide every hold, block, release and escalation. Classifying a borrower account as fraud follows the lender's board-approved process, including the borrower's right to be heard, and fraud reports to the regulator and suspicious transaction reports to FIU-IND stay with the responsible officers.

Review and growStandard3–5 weeks

Top-up and renewal journeys approved by credit

Find borrowers who meet the lender's policy for a top-up or renewal review, get the credit team's approval for the list and offer terms, and reach consented customers with a fresh, fully disclosed application.

Lending & NBFCs

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Good borrowers leave through balance transfers because nobody offers them a top-up, while ad hoc offer lists built in spreadsheets reach customers in hardship, ignore marketing consent or imply an approval credit never gave.

Trigger

A monthly LMS run for accounts that meet the policy's review criteria, or a borrower's request for more credit or a renewal, such as a gold loan nearing maturity.

How it runs

  1. Select accounts by policy criteria, such as repayment track, tenure elapsed and product rules, excluding hardship flags, restructured accounts and open complaints.
  2. Send the list and proposed offer parameters to the credit team; only accounts they approve move forward.
  3. Reach customers who gave marketing consent through approved marketing templates, 140-series promotional calls or the app, with an opt-out in every message.
  4. Capture interest and open a fresh application in the LOS with updated documents, the credit checks the lender's policy requires and a KFS; no limit rises without the borrower's explicit consent.
  5. Route each application to credit for the decision and report conversion and decline reasons by segment.

Human checkpoint

The credit team approves the review criteria, every offer list and every final decision. Offers are never presented as pre-approved unless credit has approved them, and no limit is increased without the borrower's explicit, recorded consent.
